Retrieve Hourly Time Series Data for a Given RIC

Source: R/lowlevel_wrappers.R
get_rics_h.Rd

This function retrieves 24-hour time series data for a given Reuters Instrument Code (RIC) by fetching individual hourly data. It returns a `data.table` with structured hourly data for the specified date range.

Usage

get_rics_h(rics, from_date = Sys.Date() - (365 * 10), to_date = Sys.Date())

Arguments

rics

A character string representing the base RIC (without the hour suffix) for which the data is to be retrieved.

from_date

A character or Date object representing the start date for data retrieval (default: 10 years ago).

to_date

A character or Date object representing the end date for data retrieval (default: today).

interval

A character string representing the data frequency. Defaults to `"daily"`, but is internally ignored for hourly data.

sleep

A numeric value specifying the time (in seconds) to wait between API calls (default: 0).

Value

A `data.table` containing the 24-hour data for the specified RIC, with the following columns:

  • date - Date of the observation (YYYY-MM-DD).

  • hour - Hour of the day (integer from 1 to 24).

  • ric - The base RIC identifier.

  • value - The retrieved value for the RIC.

  • volume - Trading volume or relevant metric.

Details

This function constructs RICs for each of the 24 hours by appending `01` to `24` to the base RIC. It retrieves the data, processes it into a unified table, and returns a `data.table` with hourly observations. If not all 24 hours are present, a warning is issued.

Note

If not all 24 hours are present in the dataset, a warning is issued.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
get_rics_h("HEEGRAUCH", from_date = "2020-01-01", to_date = "2023-01-01")
} # }
